http_response.description: 80-year-old woman with 6-month history of slowly increasing asymptomatic lumbar subcutaneous mass. History of chronic renal failure requiring dialysis three times weekly for 10 years. Poor compliance with phosphate-binding medications and dietary restrictions. Physical exam showed firm, immobile subcutaneous nodule measuring 9 cm in major axis. Laboratory findings: serum calcium 1.95 mmol/L (normal: 2.05-2.55), serum phosphorus 3.3 mmol/L (normal: 0.74-1.52), serum intact parathyroid hormone 142 ng/L (normal: 10-65), serum creatinine 787 μmol/L (normal: 53-106).

data.description: Deposition of calcium-phosphate salts in periarticular or subcutaneous soft tissues, typically in patients with end-stage renal disease and hyperphosphatemia, often associated with secondary hyperparathyroidism.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic renal failure on long-term dialysis
Poor compliance with phosphate binders/dietary restrictions
Elevated PTH (142 ng/L) consistent with secondary hyperparathyroidism
Slowly enlarging, firm, immobile subcutaneous mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Lumbar location (classically periarticular near hips/shoulders, though ectopic sites can occur)

data.diagnosis: Metastatic calcinosis cutis due to secondary hyperparathyroidism
data.description: Widespread or localized calcium salt deposition in skin/subcutis from high calcium-phosphate product, commonly seen in chronic kidney disease with secondary hyperparathyroidism.
symptoms_in_common: Low-normal calcium with elevated Ca×P product
symptoms_not_in_common: Single large isolated mass rather than multiple plaques/nodules (calcinosis cutis may be multifocal)

data.description: Medial calcification of small arterioles leading to ischemia and painful necrotic skin lesions in patients with ESRD, often associated with high phosphate and secondary hyperparathyroidism.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesion is asymptomatic (calciphylaxis is typically very painful)
Firm immobile subcutaneous mass without ulceration or necrosis
No violaceous plaques, livedo, or skin breakdown reported
Single localized nodule rather than multiple lesions

data.description: Malignant tumor of mesenchymal origin presenting as a deep, firm, enlarging soft tissue mass, often painless and larger than 5 cm.
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound disturbances in calcium/phosphate/PTH are not typical features of sarcoma
Long-standing ESRD/dialysis does not specifically predispose to a single large lumbar sarcoma
Absence of overlying skin changes or systemic symptoms (though many sarcomas are asymptomatic)

data.description: Chronic deposition of monosodium urate crystals forming firm subcutaneous tophi, typically in patients with longstanding hyperuricemia and gout.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic renal failure can predispose to hyperuricemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Very large size (9 cm) is uncommon for a single tophus
Location in the lumbar subcutaneous tissue is atypical (tophi usually periarticular in hands/feet, ears, olecranon, Achilles)
No history of gout flares provided
Laboratory profile (marked hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, high PTH) does not align with gout

http_response.description: 47-year-old female presented to emergency department after being hit while skiing by another skier at high speed from behind. Immediate pain and marked general swelling of the knee joint occurred after impact. Unable to bear weight. Physical exam showed neurovascularly intact limb with no broken skin. No relevant medical, family, or social history.

data.description: Acute ligament injury often caused by pivoting or valgus stress that leads to knee instability and hemarthrosis.
symptoms_in_common: marked general swelling of the knee joint
symptoms_not_in_common: high-speed impact from behind

data.description: Injury to the PCL typically from a posteriorly directed force on the proximal tibia (e.g., dashboard injury or collision from behind), causing acute pain and swelling.

data.description: Fracture of the proximal tibial articular surface often due to high-energy trauma, associated with acute pain, joint effusion, and inability to bear weight.
symptoms_in_common: marked general swelling of the knee joint

data.description: Tear of the knee’s fibrocartilaginous meniscus, typically from twisting injuries, leading to pain and impaired weight-bearing; swelling often develops over hours.
symptoms_in_common: marked general swelling of the knee joint

immediate marked swelling (meniscal swelling is often delayed rather than immediate)

http_response.description: A 52-year-old woman presented with complaints of anal pain, constipation, and tenesmus for 3 months before being referred to the hospital. There were no relevant prior illnesses. Rectal digital examination revealed a 6-cm smooth elastic mass on the rectal posterior left side 2 cm from the anal verge. Colonoscopy showed a rectal submucosal bulging. Computed tomography scan and magnetic resonance imaging confirmed the presence of a single 6-cm well-delimited mass, compressing and infiltrating the wall of the medium to low rectum.

data.description: A mesenchymal tumor arising from interstitial cells of Cajal; rectal GISTs often present as submucosal, well-demarcated masses that can compress or invade the rectal wall and cause obstructive or pain symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: 6-cm smooth elastic mass on digital rectal exam
Mass compressing and infiltrating the mid to low rectal wall
Lesion located 2 cm from the anal verge

data.description: A malignant smooth muscle tumor of the rectum that typically presents as a large submucosal mass; it can invade locally and cause pain, constipation, and tenesmus.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging showing a well-defined mass with wall infiltration
symptoms_not_in_common: Smooth elastic consistency on digital exam (malignant lesions are often firmer/irregular)

data.description: A benign nerve sheath tumor that can arise in the rectal wall; usually well-circumscribed and submucosal, causing compressive symptoms when large.
symptoms_in_common: Smooth elastic submucosal mass on exam/colonoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging evidence of wall infiltration (schwannomas are typically non-infiltrative)

data.description: A neuroendocrine tumor arising from enterochromaffin cells; rectal NETs are usually small and submucosal, but larger lesions (>2 cm) can invade deeper layers and cause obstructive symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Low rectal location near the anal verge
symptoms_not_in_common: Very large size (6 cm) compared with typical rectal NETs
Anal pain (less common unless lesions are large)

data.description: An uncommon extranodal lymphoma involving the rectum, often presenting as a submucosal mass that may cause obstructive symptoms; can be well-circumscribed but may also infiltrate the wall.
symptoms_not_in_common: Anal pain (less typical presentation)
Smooth elastic feel on digital exam (lymphomatous masses are often firmer)

http_response.description: Two-year-four-month-old female with IUGR at birth (39 weeks, cesarean delivery for placenta failure), birth weight 1850 g, length 44.5 cm, and head circumference 31 cm, all at the 3rd percentile. At 3 months, she was evaluated for suspected hearing loss; ABR showed bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss, and hearing aids were placed at 4 months. During infancy, she had poor weight and height gain below the 3rd percentile, with otherwise normal psychomotor development (sitting at 8 months, walking at 14 months, talking at 13 months). CNS MRI was normal. Genetic testing identified a de novo heterozygous PIK3R1 variant c.1956dupT (p.Lys653*) in exon 15.

data.description: A rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in PIK3R1, characterized by intrauterine growth restriction, postnatal short stature, partial lipodystrophy, insulin resistance/diabetes, distinctive facial features, ocular findings (Rieger anomaly), delayed dentition; sensorineural hearing loss can occur in some cases.
symptoms_in_common: postnatal poor weight and height gain/short stature (<3rd percentile)
de novo heterozygous PIK3R1 truncating variant (c.1956dupT, p.Lys653*)
symptoms_not_in_common: placental failure requiring cesarean delivery
no reported lipodystrophy/insulin resistance yet (often emerges later but not noted here)
no reported ocular or dental anomalies yet

data.description: An autosomal dominant primary immunodeficiency due to specific PIK3R1 variants (often splice-site) causing PI3Kδ pathway hyperactivation; features include recurrent sinopulmonary infections, lymphadenopathy/splenomegaly, autoimmunity, growth delay, and elevated transitional/naive B cells.
symptoms_not_in_common: absence of recurrent infections
no lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly reported
no autoimmunity reported
bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss (not typical)
normal CNS MRI
normal psychomotor development

data.description: A congenital infection that can cause IUGR, microcephaly, periventricular calcifications, hepatosplenomegaly, chorioretinitis, and congenital sensorineural hearing loss; neurodevelopmental impairment varies.
symptoms_not_in_common: normal CNS MRI (no calcifications reported)
normal psychomotor development
no hepatosplenomegaly or jaundice reported
no chorioretinitis reported
presence of a de novo PIK3R1 pathogenic variant explaining features

data.description: An autosomal dominant disorder characterized by congenital sensorineural hearing loss and pigmentary abnormalities of the hair, skin, and eyes, sometimes with dystopia canthorum depending on subtype.
symptoms_not_in_common: absence of pigmentary abnormalities (not reported)
intrauterine growth restriction and persistent short stature (not typical)
normal CNS MRI (expected, but not diagnostic)
presence of a de novo PIK3R1 variant rather than typical Waardenburg genes (PAX3, MITF, SOX10, EDNRB, EDN3, etc.)

data.diagnosis: Pendred syndrome / DFNB4 with enlarged vestibular aqueduct (SLC26A4-related)
data.description: A recessive disorder featuring congenital or early-onset sensorineural hearing loss (often fluctuating/progressive) associated with enlarged vestibular aqueduct and/or Mondini malformation; thyroid enlargement (goiter) and variable thyroid dysfunction may appear later.
symptoms_in_common: bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss in infancy
symptoms_not_in_common: normal brain MRI with no inner ear malformation reported
no goiter or thyroid dysfunction reported
intrauterine growth restriction and postnatal short stature (not typical)
presence of a de novo PIK3R1 variant rather than biallelic SLC26A4 variants
